PROJECT OVERVIEW

Rethinking what frozen dessert can feel like.

Frozen dessert occupies an uncomfortable position: indulgent but guilty, or virtuous but joyless. Nouri was built around a third path — where premium ingredients, considered design and honest communication could make indulgence feel genuinely thoughtful rather than defended.

The design challenge was holding tension between appetite appeal and premium restraint. Too warm and the brand reads as playful; too minimal and it feels cold. The project explored how typography, colour, packaging structure and photography could together produce something confident and considered.

"How do you make indulgence feel like a considered choice rather than a guilty one?"

BRAND STRATEGY

A brand built around thoughtful indulgence.

01

BRAND IDEA

Indulgence, reconsidered.

Nouri's central idea is that treating yourself well and treating yourself to something delicious aren't separate things. The brand doesn't ask you to compromise — it reframes the question entirely.

02

POSITIONING

Premium frozen dessert for people who think about what they eat — without making it a performance.

Nouri sits above mass-market ice cream and beneath artisan gelato theatre. It's the brand you reach for when you want something genuinely good, without needing to justify it.

03

BRAND PROMISE

"Delicious first. Nourishing always."

The tagline is the hierarchy made explicit. Nouri leads with pleasure — then earns trust through the quality of what goes into each tub. The brand never leads with health and never obscures it.

04

BRAND PERSONALITY

Warm without being playful. Premium without being austere. Honest without being clinical.

Nouri speaks like a knowledgeable friend. Direct, considered, never over-designed. The identity reflects that — restrained where possible, confident where it counts.

GRAPHIC LANGUAGE

The Nouri graphic language is built from exactly two structural devices. Every application uses both. Nothing else is permitted.

THE WRAP

A 16% band at the top of the pack and a 26% column on the left, both in the flavour field colour. Oat holds the remaining 60%. The wrap is never decorative — it identifies. It never fills.

THE ACCENT TICK

The acute accent from the "í" in the wordmark, extracted and used independently as a bullet, separator and end mark. Always Ink on light fields; always Ivory on dark flavour fields. Never rotated, never scaled below 8pt.

PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT

Good dessert does good too.

Nouri's identity was developed alongside a real product — a 480 ml frozen dessert with 28% real mango purée, cream for aroma, and dairy protein for structure. The formulation reached "high protein" and "low fat" simultaneously without losing the eating quality a premium frozen dessert requires. The numbers improved because the formulation got smarter, not because the dessert got leaner.

FORMULATION V2.1 · Concept stage · Calculated from category-average ingredient data · Requires laboratory verification before any commercial use

Mango Bliss — lead flavour

FORMULATION V2.1

Mango Bliss is built around 28% unsweetened mango purée — Alphonso-led, single-strength, not concentrate. Below about 20%, mango stops tasting like fruit and starts tasting like a mango-flavoured thing. No flavour house closes that gap. The lemon concentrate keeps it bright and prevents 28% purée from reading as jammy. Cream is present for aroma release rather than body.

The protein comes from milk protein concentrate and whey isolate — dairy was a deliberate decision. The honest ceiling for a pea or fava protein system at premium eating quality is around 6 g per 100 g. Reaching 8.5 g without dairy is not possible without a texture cost the product can't absorb.

28.0%

Mango purée, unsweetened

Alphonso-led with Totapuri. The flavour, most of the colour, and all the fruit credibility.

7.0%

Sucrose

Clean sweetness and freezing-point depression. What keeps the tub scoopable at −18 °C.

6.0%

Cream, 38% fat

Aroma release, not bulk. The fat figure is low because cream is doing flavour work, not structural work.

6.0%

Milk protein concentrate 85

The structural backbone. Delivers most of the protein and holds water through freeze-thaw cycles.

3.5%

Soluble corn fibre

85% fibre grade. Better tolerated than inulin, and raises fibre to a real margin above the 3 g threshold.

3.5%

Skimmed milk powder

Lactose for mild sweetness and body; milk solids for texture and foam stability.

+ whey protein isolate (2%), erythritol (1%), glycerol E422 (1%), lemon juice concentrate, natural vanilla flavouring, tripotassium citrate, locust bean gum, sea salt

INGREDIENTS AS DECLARED

Water, mango purée (28%), sugar, cream (milk), milk protein concentrate (milk), soluble corn fibre, skimmed milk powder, whey protein isolate (milk), erythritol, glycerol, lemon juice concentrate, natural vanilla flavouring, potassium citrate, locust bean gum, sea salt.

15 ingredients · 14 nameable · Contains milk · NOURI Foods BV, Antwerp, Belgium

What the formulation supports

CLAIMS

The hierarchy on the pack is delicious, then flavour, then brand, then proof. The formulation is built the same way. Nothing has been added for the label: the protein is doing structural work, the fibre is doing creaminess and bulk work, and the sugar reduction is capped at the point where texture would start to suffer.

What the product can honestly say: about 44% lower in energy and over 80% lower in fat than a premium dairy ice cream, 30 g of protein per tub, 13 g of fibre — made from 15 ingredients, 14 of them nameable. A real difference, arrived at without a single claim the formulation can't support.

"High protein" and "low fat" are both available simultaneously — an unusual position for a scoopable frozen dessert. Neither of them leads on pack. They're proof, not the pitch.

"High protein"available

27.8% of energy from protein. Available and defensible — held across V2 and V2.1.

"Low fat"available

2.5 g per 100 g, with 0.5 g margin above the 3 g threshold.

"Reduced energy"available

About 44% below a stated comparator at 124 kcal per 100 g. Comparison must appear on pack.

"Source of fibre"available

3.6 g vs. 3 g threshold — now a real margin, not a marginal one. Use AOAC 2001.03 for analysis.

"Reduced sugar"available

39% below a 21 g comparator. Gained in V2.1. Requires comparison stated on pack.

"30g protein per tub"available

Factual, not a nutrition claim. Declare as 30 g — protein varies by lot.

"High fibre"not available

Requires 6 g per 100 g. Reachable but the digestive load per tub becomes unreasonable.

"No added sugar"not available

Sucrose is added. "Reduced sugar" qualifies; "no added sugar" does not.

"Plant-based", "vegan"not available

Contains milk. No route to 8.5 g protein at this eating quality without dairy.

"Guilt-free", "naturally healthy"avoid

Not permitted health claims. They also contradict the brand's own voice.

Not a regulatory assessment. All claims require confirmation against Regulation (EC) 1924/2006 by a qualified adviser using analysis of real production samples.

PACKAGING

The identity becomes tangible.

The tub is where every identity decision faces physical reality. Packaging must work in a freezer cabinet at distance, in hand at close range, and on a phone screen in a product listing. The hierarchy was designed to resolve clearly at every scale.

Tub packaging

01

Information hierarchy

02
01

Wordmark

The custom-drawn "nouri" wordmark anchors the front face. Large enough to read instantly at freezer distance while remaining elegant rather than loud.

02

Flavour name

The flavour name in Vollkorn Display, set large. It functions as a colour signal from a distance before the customer reaches the freezer.

03

Ingredient cue

A short taste description in Hanken Grotesk. Communicates character — not a declaration. Appetite appeal, not a label.

04

Back panel

Full ingredient list, nutrition facts, and supporting copy. Structured with IBM Plex Mono for data and Hanken Grotesk for copy. Honest, not clinical.

Back panel

03

The back panel is designed last and read first. It carries every legal obligation the front face deliberately avoids — full ingredient list, allergen callouts, nutrition table, storage and preparation instructions, net weight, and producer details — without becoming a wall of information.

The Oat Deep field creates a recessive zone that the eye reads as technical, not decorative. Type sits in the IBM Plex Mono data hierarchy at 6 pt minimum with ample leading. Allergens appear in bold within the continuous ingredient list, not isolated into a secondary box, which gives more space to what matters: ingredient transparency.

"Good dessert does good too." runs as the closing line — the brand's promise stated plainly after all the proof has been given.

ART DIRECTION

Photography carries the appetite appeal.

The photography direction was built around three modes: texture macro, ingredient stills and product in context. Each has a specific role. Together they carry warmth and appetite appeal in ways that typography and colour cannot do alone.

[TEXTURE MACRO — MANGO BLISS]

Three photography modes

DIRECTION

[TEXTURE MACRO — DETAIL]

TEXTURE MACRO

Close-in shots of the dessert surface. These images communicate richness and quality before the customer has read a word.

[INGREDIENT STILL — MANGO]

INGREDIENT STILLS

Single-ingredient photography on clean grounds. Honest and direct — these tell you exactly what's inside without decoration.

PRODUCT IN CONTEXT

The product placed in environments that feel premium but unpretentious. Surface, light and proportion over styling.

PHOTOGRAPHY PRINCIPLES

Asymmetric crops

Images are never centred symmetrically. Off-axis compositions and deliberate negative space keep the aesthetic editorial rather than catalogue.

Natural, directional light

Hard fill light and visible product styling are avoided. Light from a single direction creates depth and warmth.

Tactile surfaces

Props and surfaces chosen for texture — stone, wood, linen — reinforce the brand's premium and grounded character.

Appetite first

Every image leads with the visual pleasure of the product. Nutrition is a back-panel argument, not a photography brief.

[CAMPAIGN COMPOSITION — EDITORIAL]

DESIGN SYSTEM

A system designed to stay recognizable.

Nouri's identity is built as a rule-based system rather than a fixed set of executions. New flavours, new formats and new contexts should be able to extend the system without requiring a designer to approve every decision.

COLOUR

One flavour colour per pack — never mix flavour colours. Type on the field follows a fixed rule: Ink on Mango, Banana, Coconut; Ivory on Strawberry, Berry, Cocoa.

TYPOGRAPHY

Vollkorn Display → Hanken Grotesk Text → IBM Plex Mono Data. Never mix Display and Mono at the same hierarchy level. Mono always uppercase, tracked 0.08–0.16em.

GRAPHIC

The Wrap and the Accent Tick are the only two graphic devices. Both appear on every pack. Nothing else is added.

WORDMARK

Primary on Oat. Reversed on Ink. Never placed on a flavour field. Minimum 24mm in print, 120px on screen. Clear space equal to cap-height on all sides.

NEUTRAL CORE

Oat is the brand field. Ivory for reversed type. Oat Light for cards and lifts. Oat Deep for nutrition panels and supporting information blocks. Ink for all type and all rules — never pure black.

BRAND PROMISE

Delicious first.
Nourishing always.

EXTENDING TO NEW FLAVOURS

A new flavour enters the system by selecting a Field, Deep and Tint tone, establishing a type-on-field rule, and applying The Wrap at the defined proportions. No other decisions are required.

REFLECTION

Designing the system, not just the package.

IDENTITY AS A SYSTEM, NOT A SET OF ASSETS

Nouri taught me that brand identity is fundamentally a systems problem. Every decision about typography, colour and photography only holds meaning in relation to the others — and those relationships have to survive being applied by people who aren't thinking about the system.

WHAT PACKAGING TAUGHT ME ABOUT HIERARCHY AND SCALE

Working through the tub layout changed how I think about hierarchy. What reads clearly in Figma doesn't automatically read clearly in a freezer cabinet at two metres. Scale forces you to commit. Every element either earns its place or gets cut.

BALANCING APPETITE APPEAL AND PREMIUM RESTRAINT

The central tension in the project — warm without being playful, premium without being cold — isn't resolved by a single decision. It's a combination of typeface, image, whitespace, and copy tone. Each one contributes a small amount. Getting all of them pointing in the same direction takes longer than it looks.
